page.title: Agent defaults
page.description: What agent runs do across the whole deployment. Each account can narrow it under Apps > Agents, and a repository can override it again.

keySharing.label: Share this deployment's provider keys
keySharing.on: Anybody without a key of their own runs on the keys stored under Integrations, and those accounts are billed to you.
keySharing.off: Runs only use keys people add themselves, under Account > AI provider keys. Nobody spends this deployment's providers.

sharedMachine.label: Offer a machine everybody shares
sharedMachine.on: Anybody who can start a session can open the shared machine. It has one home: what is signed in there is signed in for all of them, and the files one person leaves are the files the next one finds.
sharedMachine.off: Every session opens on a machine of its own account, with its own logins and its own files. Nobody can reach anybody else's.
sharedMachine.warning: Sign it in with an API key or a team plan. A personal Claude or ChatGPT subscription is licensed to one person, and several people working through one is what gets it suspended.

page.title: Chat
page.description: How long a message may be, what it may carry, how long it stays editable, and what a deleted one leaves behind. Answered separately for spaces, group chats and direct messages.

errors.notAScope: That is not a kind of conversation
errors.rulesNotSaved: Those limits could not be saved
errors.notAShare: That is not a way to share a file

space.label: Spaces
space.note: Channels inside a space - the rooms a team works in, and the record they leave.

group.label: Group chats
group.note: Three or more people in one conversation, outside any space.

maxMessageLength.label: Longest message
maxMessageLength.hint: Characters. Somebody with more to say than this has a note or a snippet.

maxPerMinute.label: Messages a minute
maxPerMinute.hint: Per person, per conversation. Thirty stops a flood without ever meeting somebody typing. Zero for as many as they can type.

spamGuard.label: Spam protection
spamGuard.hint: Limits loose enough that nobody talking normally meets them, there to stop clear abuse: the whole room pinged again and again, one person mentioned over and over, the same line pasted repeatedly. Each counts one person in one conversation; zero turns a single limit off.

maxRoomMentionsPerHour.label: @everyone and @here
maxRoomMentionsPerHour.hint: Messages carrying either that one person may send in an hour. Whoever moderates the room is not held by it.

maxMentionsPerMessage.label: People mentioned in one message
maxMentionsPerMessage.hint: Different people or teams one message may mention.

maxSamePersonMentions.label: Mentioning the same person
maxSamePersonMentions.hint: Messages mentioning the same person that one account may send in ten minutes.

maxRepeatedMessages.label: The same message again
maxRepeatedMessages.hint: How many times the very same message may be sent in two minutes.

maxAttachments.label: Files on one message
maxAttachments.hint: Zero stops files being sent in this kind of conversation at all.

maxAttachmentMib.label: Biggest single file
maxAttachmentMib.hint: A file this big is streamed straight to the storage Polaris writes uploads to, so what this really sets is how much of your disks one message may take. Somebody sharing a file they already have in Drive is not bound by it at all when this instance shares by link.

editWindowMinutes.label: How long a message stays editable
editWindowMinutes.hint: Minutes after it was sent. Zero means always, which is what people expect. It covers deleting too, and never binds somebody moderating the room.

deleteLeavesTrace.label: Deleting leaves a line saying so
deleteLeavesTrace.hint: On, a deleted message reads 'This message was deleted' and replies under it still make sense. Off, the message and its files go without trace - except for one that has replies hanging off it, which would take them with it.

keepEditHistory.label: Keep what a message said before it was edited
keepEditHistory.hint: On, '(edited)' opens the earlier versions for anybody who can read the message. Off, no earlier version is recorded from then on.

driveShare.title: A file sent from Drive
driveShare.picker: What happens to a file sent from Drive

copy.label: Copied
copy.title: A copy of its own, in the conversation's store
copy.hint: Copied into the conversation, so nothing can change it and nothing can take it away. The instance keeps a second copy of every file anybody shares, and the size limit above applies to it.

link.label: Linked
link.title: Left where it is, and reached from the message
link.hint: Shared where it already is. Nothing is copied, so any size works and the limit above does not apply - but whoever owns the file can edit it or delete it under a message that has already been read, and the conversation says so on the file.

orgChat.label: Organizations may keep their own chat
orgChat.hint: An organization that takes this gets a second chat for the people in it, reached from the shelf switch in the header. Turned off, everybody shares one chat - and any organization already keeping its own has those conversations folded back into it rather than hidden.

calls.title: Where calls run
calls.intro: Every call goes through a media server, so each browser sends its camera once instead of once per person. Polaris starts one with the stack and hands it its own key, so there is nothing to set up; until it answers, Chat says calls are unavailable rather than offering one that reaches nobody.

detail.unprepared: Calls have nowhere to run on this deployment yet. Nothing to do here: it repairs itself the next time Polaris starts, and this says so as soon as it has.
detail.missing: Its container was never created here, which is why this said it was starting and never finished. Updating again brings it up - <link>Settings</link>, Update.
detail.stopped: Its container exists and is not running. Start it from <link>Containers</link>, on the row named {container}.
detail.running: Calls between devices on this network work now. For calls from outside, two ports have to reach this machine - <link>Domains</link> lists them and reports when they answer.
detail.waited: It has had a couple of minutes and has not come up. It keeps trying, and calls come back on their own the moment it answers.
detail.starting: It comes up a few seconds after the stack does.

unused.noKey: The address below has no key saved with it, so it signs nothing and is not in use. Fill it in and save.
unused.neither: The address below has no key and secret saved with it, so it signs nothing and is not in use. Fill both in and save.

certificate.body: LAN hostnames can't get a public certificate, so Polaris signs its own. Install this root certificate on your devices once to make https://polaris.local trusted with no browser warning. macOS/iOS: open it and trust it in Keychain / Profiles. Windows: import into "Trusted Root Certification Authorities". Firefox: import under Authorities.

errors.range: The {protocol} range has to read like 25565-25664, stay above 1024, and leave 80 and 443 alone.

call.title: Call ports
call.description: Setting a call up goes through 443 with everything else. The sound does not: it arrives on the two ports below. Most calls need neither forwarded: the call server reaches out first and the reply comes back the way it went. Forward them for the networks where that does not hold.
call.checking: Checked while this page is open: the TCP port is ticked as soon as it answers from outside.
call.notAnswering: The call server is not answering, so nothing here can be checked yet.
call.unprobeableTitle: Nothing answers an unsolicited packet on this port, so it cannot be tested from here. Calls do not depend on it: the call server reaches out first, and forwarding it only helps on networks where that does not work
call.stoppedTitle: A call server that is not answering is silent on every port, so this cannot be checked from here
call.stoppedNote: The call server is not answering, so these ports carry nothing yet and cannot be checked. Chat settings says what it is doing.
call.onlyLocal: Calls only reach this network so far
call.nothingArrived: Nothing has arrived on the call ports from outside yet. Forwarding them in the router fixes it, and this ticks itself the moment they work.
call.addressStale: The call server is handing out an old address
call.address: The address callers are sent to
call.addressStaleBody: This line's public address has changed since the call server last started, so the sound is being sent to an address that is no longer this one. The port forwarding is not the problem. Restarting it is.
call.addressBody: The call server asks for it once, when it starts, and hands it out until it restarts. If this line's address changes, calls from outside go quiet while everything here stays green.
call.repairFailed: That could not be done from here.
call.repair: Ask for this network's address again

game.title: Game server ports
game.description: Ports 80 and 443 carry every website Polaris serves and not one game client. Each server below answers on its own port, on its own transport, and nothing above this opens them.
game.range: Polaris keeps them inside <tcp>TCP {tcpRange}</tcp> and <udp>UDP {udpRange}</udp>, so forwarding those two ranges covers the servers you have and the ones you have not created yet.
game.checking: Checked while this page is open, on the servers that are running: a port is ticked as soon as it answers from outside, or as soon as somebody joins on it.
game.stoppedTitle: A stopped server answers nothing, so its port cannot be checked from here
game.outside: {count, plural, one {One server answers} other {# servers answer}} outside those ranges - {names} - so {count, plural, one {it keeps} other {they keep}} a rule of their own above. Widening a range does not move a server that is already running; recreating it does.

policy.howAria: How the router is asked to open game ports
policy.invalid: A range reads like 25565-25664, stays above 1024, and cannot contain 80 or 443.

hints.range: Two rules cover every server here, now and later. Nothing outside these ranges is opened.
hints.perPort: Exact, but every new server needs another rule in the router.

danger.status: {kind, select, suspended {Suspended {at}, back {until}} other {Banned {at}}}{hasReason, select, yes {: {reason}} other {}}
danger.hint: Either one signs them out everywhere at once. A suspension lifts itself when its time is up; a ban stays until somebody lifts it.
danger.deleteHint: Deleting takes everything the account owns with it.

role.title: Role
role.hint: What they may do across Polaris. One role each, and anything narrower is a policy or access to one particular thing.
role.label: Their role

groups.title: Groups
groups.hint: Membership only. What a group may do comes from the policies attached to it.

policies.title: Policies
policies.hint: Attached directly to this account. The documents themselves are written under Policies.

resources.title: On specific things
resources.hint: Access to one server, project or space, given outside their role.
resources.empty: Nothing. What they reach is whatever their role, groups and policies allow.
resources.detail: {actions}{via, select, yes { - via {principal}} other {}}{until, select, yes { - until {date}} other {}}
resources.confirmDescription: They lose {name} the next time a page loads. Nothing else about their account changes.
resources.noAnswer: Polaris did not answer. Reload the page and try again.

capabilities.title: Capabilities
capabilities.hint: What this account may do, one thing at a time. Each follows their role unless it is set here.
capabilities.admin: This account is an administrator, which allows everything. Anything switched off here takes effect only if that is taken away first.
capabilities.label: {label} for this account
capabilities.denyTitle: Always off, whatever their role says

errors.accessFailed: Could not work out their access

link.label: Invite link
link.hint: You copy the link and send it however you like.

magic.label: Magic link by email
magic.hint: Polaris emails the link to the address you invited.

code.label: Invitation code
code.hint: A short code they type in at the sign-in page.

usersInvite.title: Invite someone
usersInvite.description: They set their own name and password when they join. The invite is good for 7 days.
usersInvite.roleNoApp: Opens no app. The account exists so they can be identified - at a share link, a drop point, or anywhere that asks for a Polaris sign-in.
usersInvite.roleHint: What each role may do is set under Management > Roles.
usersInvite.noMail: Needs an email channel: nominate one under Integrations.

otp.title: One-time password
otp.hint: Asked for on top of the link or code. Send it another way, so a misdelivered invite is not enough on its own.

where.title: Where they may connect from
where.hint: Bounds the invite and stays on the account afterwards, as a limit they cannot lift themselves. Leave empty for no restriction.

usersInvite.summaryNone: No one-time password, no address or country limits.
usersInvite.summarySet: One-time password or connection limits are set.

issued.readCode: Read this code out to them:
issued.sendError: The invite was created, but Polaris could not email it: {error}
issued.shownOnce: This is shown once. Polaris keeps only a hash of it, so it cannot be looked up again.

page.title: Settings
page.description: General configuration for this Polaris deployment.

source.label: Update with
source.imageHint: Downloads the build GitHub already made. Fastest, and it is the build every other deployment runs.
source.buildHint: Advances the checkout on the host and builds the image there. Slower, and it needs room to build, but it installs the branch as it stands instead of waiting for a published build.

schedule.label: Install updates
schedule.immediate: As soon as one is published
schedule.offHint: Everyone who can update Polaris is told when a build is ready. Nothing installs on its own.
schedule.immediateHint: A published build installs itself. The dashboard keeps serving while it rolls over.
schedule.dailyHint: Installs at the first {at} after a build appears. If Polaris is off then, it installs when it comes back.

updates.title: Updates
updates.availableBehind: Update available - {count, plural, one {{shown} commit} other {{shown} commits}} behind {branch}.
updates.blocked: The build this would install failed its checks.
updates.blockedWithLink: The build this would install failed its checks. <link>See what failed</link>
updates.building: {count, plural, one {{shown} commit} other {{shown} commits}} waiting on a build. Nothing is happening on this deployment; the update appears here once the image is published.
updates.buildingNew: New commits waiting on a build. Nothing is happening on this deployment; the update appears here once the image is published.
updates.unknown: Update state unknown (this build carries no commit reference).
updates.viewChanges: <link>View changes</link> before installing, or update now - the dashboard stays up while it rolls over.
updates.manual: Run polaris update on the host to pull the latest images and redeploy.

run.starting: The update is starting; waiting for it to report.
run.reattached: Reattached to an update already running.
run.neverReported: An update was running at {at} and never reported a result. It may still be going, or it may have been cut off.
run.lastFailed: The last update failed (exit code {code}). See the log below.
run.reportFailed: Could not prepare the report. The log above can be attached to an issue by hand.
run.started: The dashboard keeps serving while the new build starts; this page reloads when it takes over.
run.unavailable: This deployment does not install its own updates; it is updated from the machine it runs on.
run.disabled: Auto-update is disabled on this host.
run.unreachable: Couldn't reach the host agent. Use the manual command below.
run.slow: This is taking longer than expected. The log above is still the live one.
run.noLiveLog: Updating - this host writes no live log. Reconnecting when Polaris is back...
run.serving: The new build is serving - reloading...
run.failed: Update failed (exit code {code}). See the log below.
run.failedUnknown: Update failed (exit code unknown). See the log below.

log.title: Update log
log.reportNote: The report opens a prefilled issue with this log, your build, server type and domain. Nothing is sent until you submit it.

publicPages.title: Public pages
publicPages.intro: Everything else here is behind the login. These three are not, because a service you register an OAuth client with will not verify one it cannot read - Google refuses a home page behind a sign-in, and asks for the privacy policy and terms on the same domain.
publicPages.contactHint: An address or a link, shown on the privacy and terms pages as the way to reach whoever runs this deployment. Left empty, those pages carry no contact at all.

transfer.title: Move to another machine
transfer.intro: Everything this Polaris knows - accounts, services, settings and secrets - in one file, sealed with a passphrase. Sessions and metrics stay behind.
transfer.exported: Exported {count, plural, one {{shown} row} other {{shown} rows}}.{unreadable, plural, =0 {} other { {unreadableShown} saved secrets could not be opened here and will need entering again.}} Without the passphrase the file cannot be opened.
transfer.importIntro: On a fresh install: read an export in. It replaces every account and setting here, this one included.
transfer.uploadFailed: The file could not be uploaded
transfer.summary: Exported {when}: {rows, plural, one {{rowsShown} row} other {{rowsShown} rows}} in {tables, plural, one {{tablesShown} table} other {{tablesShown} tables}}, {secrets, plural, one {{secretsShown} secret} other {{secretsShown} secrets}}.
transfer.unreadable: {count, plural, one {{shown} secret} other {{shown} secrets}} could not be opened where it was exported and will need entering again.
transfer.skipped: Skipped, this version does not have them: {tables}.

errors.notASource: That is not a way of updating Polaris.
errors.transferFailed: That did not work. Nothing was changed.
errors.passphraseTooLong: That passphrase is longer than it needs to be
errors.wrongPassphrase: The passphrase is wrong, or the file has been changed
errors.confirmReplace: Confirm that everything here is replaced
errors.uploadExpired: That upload has expired. Upload the file again.
